name: software-engineer
description: Software engineering fundamentals: programming concepts, data structures, algorithms, version control, testing, debugging, and software development lifecycle. Built on top of high-school-graduate base.

facts.fact: A variable is a named storage location in memory that holds a value which can change during program execution
A data type defines what kind of value a variable can hold, such as integer, floating-point, string, or boolean
A function is a reusable block of code that performs a specific task and can take inputs (parameters) and return outputs
A conditional statement (if/else) executes different code paths depending on whether a condition is true or false
A loop repeats a block of code multiple times, with common types including for loops, while loops, and do-while loops
An array is a collection of elements stored at contiguous memory locations, accessible by index starting at 0
A string is a sequence of characters, and string manipulation includes concatenation, slicing, and searching
A boolean expression evaluates to true or false and uses operators like AND, OR, and NOT
Scope determines where a variable is accessible in a program, with local variables only visible within their function and global variables visible everywhere
Recursion is when a function calls itself to solve a smaller instance of the same problem, requiring a base case to stop
facts.query: recursion function calls itself base case

facts.fact: A linked list is a linear data structure where each element (node) points to the next, allowing dynamic size but O(n) access
A stack is a LIFO (last in first out) structure with push and pop operations
A queue is a FIFO (first in first out) structure with enqueue and dequeue operations
A hash table (hash map) stores key-value pairs and provides average O(1) lookup, insertion, and deletion
A binary tree is a hierarchical structure where each node has at most two children called left and right
A binary search tree maintains the property that left children are smaller and right children are larger than the parent
A graph is a data structure consisting of vertices (nodes) connected by edges, which can be directed or undirected
A heap is a tree-based structure that satisfies the heap property, used for priority queues
Big O notation describes the time complexity of an algorithm as input size grows, such as O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n squared)
Space complexity measures the amount of memory an algorithm uses relative to input size
Binary search finds an element in a sorted array in O(log n) time by repeatedly dividing the search range in half
Bubble sort compares adjacent elements and swaps them, running in O(n squared) time in the worst case
Merge sort divides the array in half, sorts each half recursively, then merges them, running in O(n log n) time
facts.query: merge sort divide merge O(n log n)

facts.fact: Quicksort picks a pivot, partitions elements around it, and recurses, with average O(n log n) time but worst case O(n squared)
facts.query: quicksort pivot partition O(n log n)

facts.fact: Depth-first search (DFS) explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking, using a stack or recursion
facts.query: depth first search DFS backtrack stack

facts.fact: Breadth-first search (BFS) explores all neighbors at the current level before moving deeper, using a queue
facts.query: breadth first search BFS queue neighbors

facts.fact: Dynamic programming solves problems by breaking them into overlapping subproblems and storing results to avoid recomputation
Greedy algorithms make locally optimal choices at each step, hoping to find a global optimum
A hash function maps data of arbitrary size to fixed-size values, used in hash tables and cryptographic applications
Time-space tradeoff means using more memory can reduce computation time, and vice versa
Git is a distributed version control system that tracks changes to files and enables collaboration among developers
A repository (repo) is a directory that Git tracks, containing project files and the full revision history
A commit is a snapshot of changes saved to the repository history, with a message describing what changed
A branch is a parallel line of development that diverges from the main branch, allowing isolated work
A merge combines changes from one branch into another, resolving any conflicts that arise
A pull request (PR) is a proposal to merge changes from one branch into another, enabling code review before merging
Git clone creates a local copy of a remote repository
Git push sends local commits to a remote repository, and git pull fetches and merges remote changes
A merge conflict occurs when two branches modify the same lines and must be resolved manually before merging
A .gitignore file tells Git which files and directories to exclude from version control
The Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) is the process of designing, developing, testing, and deploying software
Agile methodology breaks work into short iterations called sprints, typically 1-4 weeks, with continuous feedback
Waterfall methodology follows a linear sequence of phases: requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment, maintenance
Scrum is an Agile framework with defined roles (Scrum Master, Product Owner, Developer), ceremonies (standup, sprint planning, retrospective), and artifacts (backlog, sprint)
Continuous Integration (CI) automatically builds and tests code changes when they are committed to version control
Continuous Deployment (CD) automatically deploys code changes to production after passing CI tests
Code review is the practice of having other developers review code changes before they are merged, improving quality and sharing knowledge
Technical debt is the implied cost of future rework caused by choosing an easy solution now instead of a better approach
A user story describes a feature from the user's perspective, typically in the format: As a [role], I want [feature], so that [benefit]
Refactoring is the process of restructuring existing code to improve its readability and maintainability without changing its behavior
Unit testing verifies that individual functions or components work correctly in isolation
Integration testing verifies that multiple components work correctly together
End-to-end (E2E) testing verifies the entire application flow from start to finish, simulating real user behavior
facts.query: end to end testing application flow

facts.fact: Test-driven development (TDD) writes tests before writing the code, following the red-green-refactor cycle
facts.query: TDD test driven red green refactor

facts.fact: A bug is an error, flaw, or fault in a program that causes it to produce incorrect or unexpected results
A debugger is a tool that allows developers to pause execution, inspect variables, and step through code line by line
A stack trace shows the sequence of function calls leading to an error, helping identify where the problem occurred
Logging records events and errors during program execution, which is essential for diagnosing issues in production
A test fixture sets up the initial conditions and data needed for tests to run consistently
Code coverage measures the percentage of code that is exercised by tests, helping identify untested paths
HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the protocol for transferring web data, with methods like GET (retrieve), POST (create), PUT (update), and DELETE (remove)
facts.query: HTTP GET POST PUT DELETE methods

facts.fact: REST (Representational State Transfer) is an architectural style for APIs that uses HTTP methods and resource URLs
JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a lightweight data format using key-value pairs, commonly used for API data exchange
facts.query: JSON data format key value API

facts.fact: An API (Application Programming Interface) defines how software components communicate, specifying endpoints, methods, and data formats
The frontend is the user-facing part of an application (HTML, CSS, JavaScript), and the backend is the server-side logic and data handling
A database stores application data, with relational databases using tables (SQL) and NoSQL databases using documents or key-value pairs
CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) controls the visual presentation and layout of web pages
Authentication verifies who a user is (login), while authorization determines what they are allowed to do (permissions)
A web framework provides reusable code and patterns for building web applications, such as React for frontend and Express or Django for backend
Responsive design ensures web pages adapt to different screen sizes using flexible layouts and media queries
facts.query: responsive design screen size media query
